description: Linn County replaced its utility-scale solar moratorium with siting rules in its Unified Development Code: solar equipment 300 ft from dwellings unless the owner waives it, 120 ft from perennial streams and ditches, 50 ft from property lines in the Renewable Energy overlay district; battery storage 200 ft from property lines and rights-of-way and 500 ft from off-site occupied structures unless waived; 55 dBA day and 50 dBA night noise limits; RE overlay rezoning and a passing score on the county's solar scorecard. Concentrating solar power is prohibited, and fenced arrays over 160 acres need a wildlife corridor.
mechanism_detail: setback: solar panels, structures and electrical equipment (excluding fences and interconnection lines) 300 ft from dwellings unless the owner waives it in writing (recorded); 120 ft from the centerline of perennial stream corridors and open ditches; 50 ft from property lines in the Renewable Energy overlay district (may be reduced to zero next to another overlay use). Battery energy storage: 200 ft from a property line or right-of-way; 500 ft from the nearest property line including an occupied structure off the subject property, reducible to 200 ft by a recorded, notarized waiver from that owner; 120 ft from perennial stream corridors and open ditches; sited inside a new solar facility when built with one. overlay_zone: rezoning to the Renewable Energy overlay district and the minimum passing threshold on the Linn County Utility Scale Solar Scorecard. noise_limit: hourly average 55 dBA by day (sunrise to sunset) and 50 dBA at night (sunset to sunrise) at the occupied dwelling of an adjacent residential property, or ambient Leq plus 5 dBA where ambient is higher; neighbours may waive in writing. Other: concentrating solar power (CSP) systems prohibited; fenced array areas over 160 acres require a wildlife corridor; panels at least 24 in. above ground at maximum tilt.
evidence_text: Solar panels, structures, and electrical equipment, excluding fences and power lines for interconnection, shall be kept a minimum of three hundred (300) feet from dwellings, unless the property owner waives the setback. Waiver must be in writing and recorded.

description: Breckinridge County, Kentucky Ordinance 2025-0121 (Solar Energy Systems), second reading Feb. 17, 2025 (4-3), repealed and replaced Ordinance 2022-0321. Scope, 7-218(b): "This section applies only to a solar energy generating station that: (1) has the capacity to produce more than 1 megawatt ... (2) (i) is designed to produce electricity for sale on the wholesale market; (ii) is a community solar energy generating system ...; or (iii) is part of aggregate net metering ...; and (3) is not located on a rooftop, carport, or brownfields site or behind the meter of a retail electric customer." So rooftop, carport, brownfield and behind-the-meter stations over 1 MW remain under the county limits, as do principal-use systems from 100 kW to 1 MW. Override, 7-218(h)(1): "Except as provided in paragraphs (3) and (4) of this subsection, a local jurisdiction may not: (i) adopt zoning laws or other laws or regulations that prohibit the construction or operation of solar energy generating stations; or (ii) deny site development plans for solar energy generating stations that meet the requirements of subsection (f)"; (h)(2)(ii) requires plans up to 5 MW to be processed "as a permitted use". State siting limits of its own: 7-218(h)(3) says a ground-mounted station over 5 MW "may not be located on any lot, parcel, or tract of land that, as of January 1, 2025, is located within: (i) a Tier 1 or Tier 2 mapped locally designated growth area ...; (ii) a medium density residential area or high density residential area ...; or (iii) a mixed-use area with a residential component"; 7-218(h)(4) limits stations in a priority preservation area established before 2025-01-01 "in area to 5% of the total acreage of the priority preservation area"; and 7-218(f) requires 150 ft from the nearest wall of a residential dwelling, 100 ft from property lines, and an average height of not more than 15 ft (agricultural co-use exempt from the height rule). Grandfathering, SB 931 Section 5: "Section 1 of this Act may not be applied or interpreted to have any effect on or application to the construction or modification of a solar energy generating system that was submitted for a certificate of public convenience and necessity from the Public Service Commission or a required permit from a local government before July 1, 2025." description: Durham's Solar Energy Systems Ordinance, adopted by the Town Council on 2023-02-06 and codified in Zoning Ordinance Chapter 175 (section 175-53 Table of Uses and section 175-109.N), treats utility-scale solar as a principal use. description: Nicholas County Fiscal Court Ordinance No. 06/2024-Solar (Solar Energy System Installation Requirements), passed on second reading June 14, 2024 (6-0). It requires a county Solar Energy System License for intermediate-scale and large-scale ground-mounted solar in all unincorporated areas of Nicholas County, Kentucky, and sets the solar footprint back at least 2,000 feet from any non-participating property line and any right-of-way of a publicly maintained road or rail line.
mechanism_detail: setback: Intermediate-Scale and Large-Scale SES footprint no less than 2,000 ft from any non-participating property line and any right-of-way for a publicly maintained roadway or rail line, measured from the property line of the non-participating property or the boundary of the public roadway or rail line to the nearest portion of the SES footprint. License: a Nicholas County Solar Energy System License is required before physical construction or enlargement ($250 review fee; the fiscal court recommends within 60 days and the Judge/Executive issues, denies or remands within 30 days; a renewal license with each decommissioning plan update). Scope: all unincorporated areas of Nicholas County; Intermediate-Scale = ground-mounted footprint of 2,501 sq ft up to and including 40 acres that is not a merchant electric generating facility; Large-Scale = footprint over 40 acres or any non-exempt SES that is a merchant electric generating facility under KRS 278.700(2); integrated, rooftop and small-scale (2,500 sq ft or less) systems exempt. Also an 8 ft fence with a double row of staggered evergreens (5 ft at planting, maturing to at least 15 ft; 90% opacity to 8 ft within 3 years), a decommissioning plan updated at least every 5 years with a surety, and decommissioning to begin within 12 months after generation ceases. Penalty: misdemeanor, $100 to $500 per violation, each day a separate offense.
evidence_text: "Setbacks. The SES footprint shall be setback no less than 2,000 feet from any non-participating property line and any right-of-way for a publicly maintained roadway or rail-line." (Ordinance No. 06/2024-Solar, Section 4.A.1); "Prior to the commencement of physical construction or enlargement of an Intermediate-Scale SES or Large-Scale SES, the responsible entity (applicant) must obtain a Nicholas County Solar Energy System License." (Section 3.A); "Date of Second Reading and Passage: 06/14/24 ... Vote: 6-0"

description: City of Pasadena, Texas Ordinance 2025-205 (adopted October 21, 2025; in effect January 19, 2026) adopts the 2024 International Fire Code with local amendments and repeals Ordinance 2025-082. Its new Section 1208 sets siting rules for battery energy storage (BESS) sites: no larger than five acres; at least 1,500 feet from another BESS site and 1,000 feet from critical facilities; structures and equipment set back 150 feet from rear and side property lines and 50 feet from the right of way; no site in a special flood hazard area; and a Special Use Permit and CenterPoint Energy approval.
mechanisms: setback; cap on acreage; zoning restriction
mechanism_detail: 5 acre maximum BESS site, measured property line to property line, excluding setback areas (Sec. 1208.4(a)); 150 ft from rear and side property lines for all structures, buildings and equipment (1208.4(b)); 1,500 ft from another BESS site, measured from the nearest property line (1208.4(c)); 1,000 ft from all critical facilities (Sec. 1202.1: hospitals, nursing homes, police and fire stations, emergency operations centers, utility facilities, hazardous materials facilities, water and wastewater plants), excluding other BESS sites and CenterPoint Energy facilities, measured from the nearest property line (1208.4(d)); 50 ft from the right of way (1208.4(e)); no BESS site in a special flood hazard area (1208.4(f)); Land Use Request (1208.1), Special Use Permit (1208.3(4)) and CenterPoint Energy review and approval before a City permit (1208.3(8))
evidence_text: 1208.4 Site Location. The site location for the installation of Solar Photovoltaic System Arrays, Energy Storage Systems, Dedicated-Use Buildings and any other buildings or structures that contain or are otherwise associated with a BESS shall comply with the following: (a) BESS sites shall be no larger than five (5) acres in size, measured property line to property line; excluding setbacks areas as described in (d) and (f). (b) All structures, buildings, and equipment shall be setback a minimum of one-hundred fifty (150) feet from rear and side property lines. All setbacks shall be sodded or seeded and comply with all current City landscaping codes. (c) BESS sites shall be no closer than fifteen-hundred (1,500) feet from another BESS site measured from nearest property line. (d) BESS sites shall be no closer than one thousand (1,000) feet from all critical facilities; excluding other BESS sites and Centerpoint Energy facilities, measured from the nearest property line. (e) All structures, buildings, and equipment shall be setback a minimum of fifty (50) feet from the right of way. (f) BESS sites shall not be located in a special flood hazard area.

description: La Paz County Zoning Regulations 2012 (Ordinance No. 2011-05, adopted December 5, 2011, effective January 5, 2012), Section 619.00, PU Public Utilities Zoning District.
